key_insight: A Transformer-based on-policy actor–critic can progressively focus exploration on hierarchical reward structure and achieve minimax-optimal learning rates for RL post-training, while offline sampling can be fundamentally slower.
engineering_relevance: For language-model post-training, this suggests that coupling KL-regularized exploration with a neural critic can be more sample-efficient than fixed-distribution reward modeling when rewards are sparse or multi-stage.
method: Model reward as an infinite hierarchy of local components that only matter after earlier components are solved.
Alternate between on-policy sampling from a KL-regularized policy, fitting a Transformer critic to observed rewards, and updating the policy.
Analyze query-budget and regularization-dependent regret/rate guarantees; compare against fixed-reference (offline) sampling.
evidence_signal: The paper provides theory-only evaluation, proving minimax-optimal rates up to logarithmic factors and showing offline-style fixed reference sampling can be limited to logarithmic regret decay.
watch_item: The guarantees are theoretical and depend on the hierarchical reward assumption, so practical gains may vary if real reward signals are not strongly hierarchical or the critic is misspecified.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning for Hierarchical Reasoning Rewards: Minimax-Optimal Rates with Transformers
